messages:
maria: heads-up — saw a 12-18% throughput regression on H100 (sm92) after switching the default fp8 kernel path for seq_len >= 2048. KV warmup + continuous batching seems to trigger it.

perf-bot: automated job 2026-03-10T22:04Z results:
- config: fp8-path=true, kv_warmup=true, batching=continuous
- throughput tokens/s: 72k (baseline int8=86k)
- p95 latency: 132ms (baseline 118ms)

maria: attaching the lightweight profile snippet I captured on node-3: 
```
Kernel selector: picked fp8_conv_v2 for layer 5..12
KV cache: warmup hit rate 0.92
Batcher: avg batch size 3.4 -> 6.8 during long tails
CUDA timelines: kernel fp8_conv_v2 launches increased stalls (SM utilization 62% -> 48%)
Time breakdown (ms): attention_fp8 54, kv_fetch 12, fused_ffn_fp8 38, memcpy 6
```

shiv: hmm. does the int8 kernel use a different tiling that benefits long seqs? also wondering if workspace allocation patterns changed with fp8 path.

alex: can you paste the kernel names with workspace sizes? I suspect a workspace growth that causes more L2 thrash at large batches.

maria: here: 
```
fp8_conv_v2: workspace=24MB, sm_version=92, tile=128x64
int8_conv_v1: workspace=12MB, sm_version=92, tile=64x64
```

ben: that workspace delta is huge. doubling workspace per kernel could push us over shared mem/L2 pressure when multiple warps active. explains utilization drop.

carmen: what about seq_len dependency? does selector switch earlier for smaller batches?

maria: selector currently uses rule: if arch >= sm90 and model_type == decoder and quant==fp8 -> prefer fp8_conv_v2 regardless of seq_len. we didn't gate by seq_len.

shiv: propose: introduce seqlen-aware threshold per-arch. e.g. for sm92 prefer fp8_conv_v2 only if seq_len <= 1536 OR avg_batch_tokens < 15000. otherwise fallback to int8_conv_v1.

alex: +1. also add a hysteresis window to avoid flapping when batch sizes float around threshold (e.g. 10% margin).

ben: we should run a quick matrix: arches=[sm83,sm86,sm92,sm95], seq_lens=[512,1024,1536,2048,4096], batching_modes=[continuous, burst], kv_warmup=[on,off]. I'll script it.

maria: thanks. can we also gather L2/cache eviction counters and per-kernel SM occupancy? that's the missing evidence.

perf-bot: queued microbench job ID 60192 (ben/matrix). estimated runtime 3h. will publish results to /perf/artifacts/60192.json

carmen: small UX note: for dedicated customers we need an operator knob to force fallback to int8 for longseq workloads. add flag kernel_selector.force_fallback_longseq=true/false.

shiv: good call. implementation plan: 1) add per-arch seqlen thresholds into selector config (yaml) with hysteresis 2) expose operator knob for forced fallback 3) run ben's matrix and collect perf counters 4) pick default thresholds and land gradual rollout behind feature flag.

alex: I'll add metrics hooks: selector.chosen_kernel, selector.reason (arch,seqlen,forced), kernel.workspace_bytes, kernel.sm_occupancy. export as labels for tracing.

maria: experiment priorities: run sm92-longseq with kv_warmup on/off to isolate kv effect, compare fp8 vs int8 with identical batcher settings.

ben: starting matrix now. first run: sm92 seq_len=2048 batching=continuous kv_warmup=on fp8 vs int8. posting results in ~25m.

carmen: I'll draft the operator knob doc and add examples to /docs/ops/kernel-selector.md

maria: thanks — if the matrix confirms workspace/L2 pressure, I think default should be: sm92: prefer fp8 for seq_len <=1536, fallback to int8 above. sm95 maybe larger threshold. we'll tune after data. :thumbsup:

shiv: one more idea: dynamic workspace cap per-process so fp8 kernel can be limited to N MB to avoid cross-kernel thrash. might be a safer mitigation while we finalize thresholds.

alex: noted. I'll add that as an experimental runtime flag kernel.max_workspace_mb.

perf-bot: update: job 60192 started 2026-03-10T22:15Z. live logs: /perf/live/60192

maria: great work. assign follow-ups: ben run matrix (owner), alex add metrics + workspace flag (owner), shiv implement selector config + hysteresis (owner), carmen doc + knob (owner). I'll collect results and propose defaults by EOD tomorrow.

ben: acknowledged. starting now.

alex: acknowledged.

shiv: acknowledged.

carmen: acknowledged.

maria: closing the loop here once job artifacts posted. will open a tiny PR with selector config changes after we have numbers.
